propositions: Source code comments contain unresolvable commit SHAs, run IDs, and dated incident narratives that decay over time and should be replaced with durable references to the ticket system.

A new block-level detector must identify rot-prone patterns in comments and docstrings: SHA-like hex (≥7 chars, mixed digits+letters), run/job/thread IDs (≥8 digits after keyword), and date+incident-verb combinations, with false-positive gotchas like 'bug surfaced' deliberately excluded.

Detected violations are remediated by one of three forms: cite a ticket/epic/story/bug ID resolvable in the ticket system, drop the rot-prone token and keep durable prose, or replace SHA narrative with behavioral description findable via git log.

The CI guard (check_comment_hygiene.py, wired into _build-and-test.yml) must fail on reintroduced rot-prone refs, pass the remediated tree with zero in-tree suppressions except for the detector's own unit-test module (EXCLUDED_FILES self-exclusion).

An acceptor validates that triggered blocks cite qualifying ticket IDs (hex-grouped 4x4 format or word-triple aliases) or have 'context: external' escape-hatch annotation; word-triple alias pattern must not match file paths with extensions.

Post-merge verification revealed acceptor false-accept on file-path hyphenated names and a race with new run-id refs merged after the guard landed, requiring alias-pattern refinement and two additional gotcha test cases.
